conclusion.runtime: Full frozen CPU native sidecar qualifies on both memory and prose, with2029prose documents/134queries added and all134prose top10 rankings exact.
conclusion.quality: Frozen full-prose cosine retrieval improves overall and on exact identifiers versus current Gemma; broad semantic superiority is not established. Memory cosine quality is effectively tied with Harrier at this sample power.
conclusion.hybrid: The fresh8-source-target-per-corpus hybrid validation remains inconclusive and does not reject the heldout negatives.
conclusion.latency: Existing serial warm CPU samples favor mDenseOn over Harrier on memory; prose query latency is similar to Gemma. They are single blocks, not randomized interleaved repetitions.
conclusion.adoption: Promising candidate for memory efficiency and prose identifier retrieval; production model/index switches remain outside this work.

currentLimitations: Only eight independent positive source targets per fresh heldout corpus, with three query classes each; query-level bootstrap is secondary to source-grouped bootstrap.
Agent-authored relevance labels frozen before inference; not an independent human relevance audit.
Four heldout hard negatives per corpus; every model returned at least one hybrid hit for every negative, so cosine calibration does not establish hybrid rejection.
Production canonical SQL, lexical search and fusion are exercised in PID-owned cloned schemas; neutral precomputed adapter excludes extraction, entity graph, decay and HTTP request path.
Fresh corpus is a structurally sampled 48 memory rows and 49 prose sections, not the whole live population.
Tokenizer truncation is verified at 8192; numeric graph parity controlled inference reaches 1024 tokens, not full 8192-token inference.
Timing is warm CPU latency on this host, not cold-start, GPU or full production concurrency; no causal resource-load attribution.
Candidate timing includes isolated sidecar HTTP overhead; incumbent timing uses the shipped in-process worker builders.
Three timing trials within one block per model/corpus, not interleaved randomized blocks; host time drift may affect the cross-model comparison.
No final deployed-main acceptance or live release-gate operation required or performed.
Full frozen CPU sidecar parity now covers2143documents and284queries across memory and prose; full134prose top10 rankings and class metrics exactly reproduce the Python reference.
Frozen full-prose query mix is90identifier/24lexical-gap/8intent positives; the overall gain must not be described as a universal semantic win.
Equal-source statistical sensitivity is exploratory and uses frozen relevance labels, not a new independent human relevance audit.
